name: Kinloch Varrick windstorm
summary: A violent windstorm cancels ferries, fells trees and closes the Carrick Narrows Bridge; a bridge-damage rumour is denied, a scam 'emergency hotel' link spreads and power figures are revised before the storm eases.

steps.title: Yellow wind warning
steps.description: A deepening low is forecast to bring gusts of up to 80 mph by afternoon.
steps.expect: Early advisory-level warning; ferry disruption rumours appear.

official.title: Storm Corran: warning for Kinloch Varrick and coast

alert.heading: Yellow warning: strong winds
alert.text: Gusts of 60 to 70 mph are expected on the coast from 12:00, with a risk of falling trees and disruption to travel.

sections.heading: Travel
items: Varrick Isles Ferries is running a normal timetable this morning but expects cancellations from midday.
High-sided vehicles are advised to avoid the Carrick Narrows Bridge from 12:00.

sections.heading: What to do
items: Secure garden furniture, bins and trampolines.
Charge phones and check on elderly neighbours.
Avoid walking along sea fronts and cliff paths.

news.headline: Storm Corran to hit Varrick coast this afternoon
news.standfirst: Gusts of up to 70 mph are forecast. Ferries may be cancelled from midday.
paragraphs: A yellow wind warning has been issued for Kinloch Varrick and the surrounding coast ahead of Storm Corran, which is expected to strengthen through the day.
Varrick Isles Ferries says sailings are running for now but warns that crossings after 12:00 are likely to be cancelled.
Residents are being advised to secure loose items and avoid unnecessary journeys this afternoon.

quotes.text: We have already lashed down the boats. You can feel it building.

posts.name: Fiona M.
posts.text: Wind already howling on the shore road. Not looking forward to this afternoon 😬

posts.name: Callum R.
posts.text: Heard all ferries are cancelled for the whole day already??

posts.name: Ishbel
posts.text: Garden furniture in the shed, bins roped to the fence. Ready as I'll ever be

steps.title: Upgraded to orange, ferries cancelled
steps.description: Gusts are reaching 85 mph. Ferries are cancelled and the Carrick Narrows Bridge restricts all high-sided vehicles.
steps.expect: Ferry cancellation confirmed; escalation to orange; rumours of bridge damage begin.

official.title: Storm Corran: warning for Kinloch Varrick and coast

alert.heading: Orange warning: severe winds
alert.text: Gusts have reached 85 mph. Expect widespread tree falls, structural damage and power cuts. Do not travel unless essential.

sections.heading: Ferries
items: All Varrick Isles Ferries sailings are cancelled for the rest of today.
Passengers should not travel to the terminals.

sections.heading: Roads and bridges
items: Carrick Narrows Bridge is closed to high-sided vehicles, caravans and motorbikes.
The A890 is blocked by fallen trees near Achnaban.

sections.heading: Power
paragraphs: About 6,000 homes are without electricity. Engineers cannot work in the current wind.

timeline.text: Raised to orange. Ferries cancelled. A890 blocked.

posts.name: Callum R.
posts.text: Ferries really are cancelled now, my sister is stuck on the island 😟

posts.name: Morag
posts.text: Huge tree down across the A890 at Achnaban, no way through. Photo
posts.media: photo: large fallen tree across a road

posts.name: Hamish B.
posts.text: Carrick Narrows Bridge looks like it's swaying badly, think it's cracked??

posts.name: Ishbel
posts.text: Lights flickering on and off here, expecting a cut any minute

steps.title: Red warning, bridge closed to all traffic
steps.description: The warning goes red. The bridge is closed to all traffic as a precaution; officials deny structural damage.
steps.expect: Bridge closure confirmed, damage rumour debunked, power figure rises.

official.title: Storm Corran: warning for Kinloch Varrick and coast

alert.heading: Red warning: danger to life
alert.text: Gusts of up to 95 mph are recorded. Stay indoors. Flying debris and falling trees are a danger to life.

sections.heading: Bridge closure
paragraphs: Carrick Narrows Bridge is closed to ALL traffic, including pedestrians, from 13:40 as a precaution while winds exceed safe limits. It will be inspected once wind speeds fall.

sections.heading: Roads
items: A890 blocked at Achnaban and Loch Fada.
Only emergency vehicles should be on the road.

sections.heading: Power
paragraphs: An estimated 14,000 homes are now without power. Restoration cannot begin until the wind falls.

sections.heading: Shelter
paragraphs: Kinloch Varrick Community Hall is open as a warm refuge for anyone who has lost power and cannot stay safely at home.

not_true: Reports that the Carrick Narrows Bridge is cracked or damaged are not true. The bridge is closed as a precaution only.
No evacuation of Kinloch Varrick has been ordered.

timeline.text: Red warning. Bridge closed to all traffic. 14,000 homes without power.

news.headline: Red warning as Corran peaks: bridge shut, 14,000 without power
news.standfirst: The Carrick Narrows Bridge has been closed to all traffic. Officials say it is a precaution, not damage.
paragraphs: A red warning is now in force. Gusts of 95 mph have been recorded and the partnership says there is a danger to life from flying debris.
The Carrick Narrows Bridge closed to all traffic at 13:40. Posts online claim the structure is cracked; the partnership says this is untrue and the closure is a precaution until it can be inspected.
About 14,000 homes are without power and ferries remain cancelled.

quotes.text: I have never heard the wind sound like this. We are staying in the hallway.

posts.name: Fiona M.
posts.text: Power just went out across the whole street. Hall is open for anyone who needs a warm space 🕯️

steps.title: Wind easing, power figures revised
steps.description: The red warning drops to orange. The power-cut estimate is revised down to 9,000 homes; a post claims everything is fine and roads are open.
steps.expect: De-escalation; official update changes a number; reassurance post held back.

official.title: Storm Corran: warning for Kinloch Varrick and coast

alert.heading: Orange warning: winds easing
alert.text: Gusts have fallen to 60 mph and are still easing. Dangerous conditions remain; stay off the roads.

sections.heading: Power
paragraphs: The earlier estimate was too high. About 9,000 homes (previously 14,000) are without power. Crews are starting repairs where it is safe.

sections.heading: Bridge and roads
items: Carrick Narrows Bridge stays closed until engineers inspect it at first light tomorrow.
A890 remains blocked at Achnaban and Loch Fada.

sections.heading: Ferries
paragraphs: Ferry services are not expected to resume before midday tomorrow.

sections.heading: Safety
items: Never touch fallen power lines.
Use torches, not candles, where possible.
Do not run generators indoors.

not_true: Reports that the bridge has reopened and roads are clear are not true.

timeline.text: Lowered to orange. 9,000 homes without power.

posts.name: Dougie
posts.text: Wind has dropped, bridge is open again and the roads are all clear. Come on home folks!

posts.name: Morag
posts.text: Do NOT trust that, the A890 is still blocked and the bridge is shut. I'm looking at it.
posts.media: photo: blocked road with warning lights

posts.name: Ishbel
posts.text: Hall is doing hot soup, power still off here. Thank you volunteers ❤️

posts.name: Callum R.
posts.text: Crews out on Shore Road already. Never seen them so fast

steps.title: Next morning: bridge reopens, warnings end
steps.description: Engineers reopen the bridge at first light; ferries restart at noon; most power restored.
steps.expect: All-clear: bridge reopened after inspection; warnings ended.

official.title: Storm Corran: recovery for Kinloch Varrick and coast

sections.heading: Warnings
paragraphs: All weather warnings ended at 06:00. Winds are now below 30 mph.

sections.heading: Bridge and roads
items: Carrick Narrows Bridge reopened at 07:30 after inspection. No structural damage was found.
A890 reopened at Loch Fada. Achnaban remains single lane while trees are cleared.

sections.heading: Ferries and power
items: Ferry services are due to resume at 12:00, with a reduced timetable.
About 1,800 homes remain without power; most are expected back by this evening.

timeline.text: Lowered to orange. 9,000 homes without power.

news.headline: Varrick wakes to storm clean-up as bridge reopens
news.standfirst: Engineers found no damage to the Carrick Narrows Bridge. Ferries restart at noon.
paragraphs: Carrick Narrows Bridge reopened at 07:30 after inspection, confirming officials' statements that it had not been damaged by Storm Corran.
About 1,800 homes remain without power, down from a peak of 14,000 estimated yesterday afternoon, which was later revised to 9,000.
Ferries will resume a reduced service at noon.

quotes.text: We lost a few slates and a fence, but we are lucky compared to others.
